74693.subject: Literature in English
74693.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights.

The overriding depiction of mystery and terror in the novel accounts for its classification as a
74693.explanation:
In literary analysis, Wuthering Heights is classified as a Gothic novel because it prominently features elements designed to evoke mystery, suspense and fear.

Mystery and terror are hallmarks of the Gothic genre. Here is how Emily Brontë applies these elements in the story:

  • Setting: The isolated, gloomy Yorkshire moors and the crumbling, dark house of Wuthering Heights create an atmosphere of dread.

  • The Supernatural: The novel opens with the haunting encounter of Catherine’s ghost at the window, setting a tone of mystery that persists throughout.

  • Dark Emotions: Heathcliff is a classic "Byronic hero"—brooding, vengeful, and intense—whose actions often border on the monstrous.

  • Atmosphere: Brontë uses heavy "pathetic fallacy," where the wild, stormy weather reflects the internal turmoil and terror of the characters.

74694.subject: Literature in English
74694.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel.

The chief of Ilujinle village is
74694.explanation: In the play, Baroka is the Bale (the traditional chief or "Lion") of Ilujinle village. He is a crafty 62-year-old leader who represents traditional Yoruba values and works to preserve the village's customs against modern influences.

74695.subject: Literature in English
74695.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger.

Jimmy's feeling about Alison's upper-class status is that of
74695.explanation:
In this landmark "Kitchen Sink" drama, Jimmy Porter's feelings toward his wife Alison's upper-class background are central to his character:

  • Class Struggle: Jimmy is a working-class intellectual who feels marginalised by the British establishment. He views Alison's family and her upbringing with deep resentment. He also uses her as a target for his rants against the status quo.

  • Conflict: He frequently mocks her "refined" manners and her family’s military and colonial history, seeing it as a symbol of the stagnant class system he despises.

74696.subject: Literature in English
74696.question_text:
This question is based on Literary Appreciation

A thousand explosions in the belly of the earth
Bleeding rigs, bursting pipes
The oil flows
From the earth's sickbed
Because
The oil only flows
When the earth bleeds

The subject matter of the excerpt above is
74696.explanation: The excerpt describes the violent impact of oil extraction on the environment, using phrases like "A thousand explosions in the belly of the earth," "Bleeding rigs" and "bursting pipes". The poem (identified as Nnimmo Bassey's "We Thought It Was Oil but It Was Blood") depicts the earth as a "sickbed" that "bleeds". Despoliation refers to the act of plundering or stripping a place of its value and natural beauty, which perfectly matches the

74697.subject: Literature in English
74697.explanation: The poem uses the metaphor of a "caged bird" to represent the lived experience of Black Americans. The bird’s "bars of rage" and "clipped wings" symbolise the systemic segregation and racial discrimination that restrict freedom and opportunity. The "free bird," by contrast, represents the white population who can "leap on the back of the wind."

options.text: the abolition of slavery and the freedom of caged people
the limitation of racially discriminated African Americans
the colonial invasion and slave trade

74698.subject: Literature in English
74698.question_text: The experience of the persona in Eliot's "The Journey of the Magi" is
74698.explanation: The persona (one of the Magi) describes the journey as physically gruelling, recalling "the very dead of winter" and "hostile" cities. While he admits it was a "hard and bitter agony" like death, the journey is ultimately fulfilling because it leads to a spiritual transformation. He acknowledges that he "would do it again". This shows that the spiritual "Birth" he witnessed was worth the hardship.

74699.subject: Literature in English
74699.question_text: Beauty in Donne's "The Good Morrow" represents the poet's persona's
74699.explanation: In this metaphysical poem, Donne celebrates a "waking" into a mature, spiritual love. When he mentions any "beauty" he had seen and desired before, he notes it was but a "dream" of his current lover. To him, all previous experiences of beauty were merely shadows of the real woman he now loves.

74700.subject: Literature in English
74700.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights

Take my colt, gipsy, then! said young Earnshaw...and wheedle my father out of all he has

The statement  above exemplifies
74700.explanation:
This quote ("Take my colt, gipsy, then!") occurs during the second half of the novel when Nelly Dean narrates the childhood history of Hindley and Heathcliff to Mr. Lockwood.

Because the novel begins near the end of the story and the majority of the plot is told as a retrospective story from Nelly’s memory, these scenes are examples of a flashback.

74701.subject: Literature in English
74701.question_text:
He lifted his head from his drinking
as cattles do,
And looked at me vaguely, as
drinking cattles do,
And flickered his two-forked tongue
from his lips, and mused
a moment (D.H. Lawrence)

The poetic object in the extract above is
74701.explanation: The text mentions the object "flickered his two-forked tongue from his lips". A two-forked tongue is a biological characteristic of a snake.

74702.subject: Literature in English
74702.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen

The narrative of the novel centres around
74702.explanation: The novel is semi-autobiographical and centres around Adah, a Nigerian woman. It follows her journey from Lagos to London as she struggles against gender discrimination, poverty, and an abusive marriage to Francis while striving to become a writer and a "first-class" citizen.

74703.subject: Literature in English
74703.question_text: Another form of literature that often employs verse is
74703.explanation: While prose is the language of ordinary speech, drama (plays) frequently employs verse Shakespeare’s plays are primarily written in "blank verse" (unrhymed iambic pentameter). Parables and fables are usually written in prose.

74704.subject: Literature in English
74704.question_text: An understatement for the purpose of emphasis is known as
74704.explanation: Litotes is a figure of speech that uses an understatement for emphasis by expressing an affirmative through the negation of its contrary. Saying "He is not the brightest bulb" to mean someone is unintelligent, or "It's not a bad day" to mean it is a good day.

74705.subject: Literature in English
74705.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.

I'm trying to settle how I shall pay Hindley back.
I don't care how long I will wait, if I can only do it at last. I hope he will not die before I do!                                                                   
Who made the statement?
74705.explanation: The speaker is Heathcliff, expressing his lifelong obsession with getting revenge on Hindley Earnshaw.  Hindley abused and humiliated Heathcliff throughout their childhood, and Heathcliff vows: "I'm trying to settle how I shall pay Hindley back. I don't care how long I will wait...".

74706.subject: Literature in English
74706.question_text:
This question is based on Literary Principles

The choice of words used by a writer in a literary work is called
74706.explanation: By definition, diction refers to the specific choice and use of words and phrases by a writer in a literary work.

74707.subject: Literature in English
74707.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel

I was there when it happened to your father

The line above is in reference to
74707.explanation:
In the play, this line is a pivotal part of Baroka’s (the "Lion") cunning plan to win over Sidi, the village belle. Baroka spreads a false rumour that he has become impotent. He does this to lure Sidi into a false sense of security, making her believe he is no longer a "threat" to her chastity.

When Sadiku says, "I was there when it happened to your father," she is referring to the loss of virility/potency. Sadiku was Baroka's father's last wife and was inherited by Baroka when he became king. So, she was present during his father's old age and had knowledge of his impotency

Sidi, believing Baroka is harmless, visits him to mock him, only to be seduced by his wisdom and strength. This eventually leads her to marry him instead of the schoolteacher, Lakunle.

74708.subject: Literature in English
74708.question_text:
This question is based on Literary Appreciation

The sunset steals our youth
We must depart
We must follow the trail of the killer-bird
Or else sleep the sleep of terror

The excerpt above portrays the theme of
74708.explanation: The "sunset" is a classic literary metaphor for the end of life or old age. It suggests that time is depleting our life force. "We must depart" is a direct euphemism for dying or leaving the world of the living. "Follow the trail of the killer-bird" portrays the idea of a journey toward an end.

74709.subject: Literature in English
74709.question_text: The spatial setting of Senghor's "Black Woman" is
74709.explanation:
Senghor was a pioneer of the Négritude movement, and this poem is a celebration of African identity and heritage. The poem establishes its African spatial setting through several key elements:

  • Geographical References: The speaker describes a woman whose beauty is rooted in the African landscape, using imagery of the savannah and the sun.

  • Cultural Identity: The "Black Woman" acts as a personification of the African continent itself - nurturing, beautiful, and ancient.

74710.subject: Literature in English
74710.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles

A multifaceted character in literature is regarded as
74710.explanation:
A round character is a complex and multifaceted character that possesses a depth of personality and contradictory traits. Such a character also undergoes internal development throughout a story. They are designed to feel like real people.

In contrast, a flat character is two-dimensional and is defined by a single trait or function. Such a character remains unchanged (static) throughout the narrative.

74711.subject: Literature in English
74711.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger

Jimmy's first love, who is ten years older than him, is
74711.explanation: In the play, Madeline is described as Jimmy Porter's first love, who was ten years older than him. Jimmy often reminisces about her "enthusiasm" for life, using her as a point of contrast to criticise his wife Alison's perceived passivity.

74712.subject: Literature in English
74712.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel.

No one? Do you mean there was no one
To bar unwanted strangers from my privacy?
Who made this statement?
74712.explanation: This line is spoken by Baroka, the Bale (village head). He uses this mock outrage as part of his elaborate scheme to seduce Sidi. By pretending he has no one to guard his privacy, he creates an opportunity to lure Sidi into his bedroom under the guise that he is a vulnerable, "impotent" old man.

74713.subject: Literature in English
74713.question_text:
This question is based on General Literary Principles.

Repetition is a literary device employed for the purpose of
74713.explanation: The primary purpose of repetition as a literary device is to emphasise a particular idea, feeling or theme to ensure it stays in the reader's mind.

74714.subject: Literature in English
74714.question_text:
This question is based on Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn

The narrative technique employed in the novel is
74714.explanation: The novel uses an omniscient or limited third-person narrator who refers to characters like Nii and Mama Orojo by name or as "he" and "she." This allows the author to jump between the parallel stories taking place in Ghana and Nigeria.

options.text: first and second person point of view

74715.subject: Literature in English
74715.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger

The setting of the play is
74715.explanation:
The play is set in the 1950s (Post-WWII). It is famous for being part of the "Angry Young Men" movement, which rebelled against the lingering Victorian and Edwardian values represented by Alison's family.

Though the 1950s is the era of Queen Elizabeth II, it is not commonly referred to as the Elizabethan era.

74716.subject: Literature in English
74716.question_text:
This question is based on Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.

From the events in the novel, one can conclude that Joseph is
74716.explanation: Joseph is a servant at Wuthering Heights who is strictly religious and constantly quotes the Bible to judge others. However, he is often seen as hypocritical because his "piety" is used as a weapon to be unkind, self-serving and cruel to those around him.

74717.subject: Literature in English
74717.question_text:
This question is based on Alex Agyei-Agyiri Unexpected Joy at Dawn.

The main conflict in the novel is
74717.explanation: The novel explores the social and political decay in Ghana and Nigeria. It highlights how corruption, economic mismanagement and tribalism affect the lives of ordinary citizens like Nii and Mama Orojo.

74718.subject: Literature in English
74718.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel

Lakunle is portrayed as the foil of
74718.explanation: A foil is a character who contrasts with another character to highlight particular qualities of the other character. Lakunle (the Westernised, "modern" schoolteacher) serves as a perfect foil to Baroka (the traditional, "old-fashioned" village head). Lakunle's verbosity and lack of real action contrast with Baroka's cunning, quiet strength and successful traditionalism.

74719.subject: Literature in English
74719.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class CItizen.

Adah faces discrimination based on
74719.explanation:
Adah faces systemic sexism from a young age in Nigeria. Her family initially refuses to send her to school because she is a girl, but they allow her brother Boy to go to school. Later, in her marriage, she is expected to be subservient to Francis, who resents her ambition and intellectual superiority. She is viewed primarily as a child-bearer and a source of income rather than an individual with her own rights.

When Adah moves to the United Kingdom, she encounters the harsh reality of being a "second-class citizen" due to her race. This is most vividly illustrated through:

  • Housing struggles: The "Sorry, No Coloureds" signs she encounters while searching for an apartment.

  • Employment: The difficulty in finding work that matches her high level of education and library experience because she is Black.

  • Social Isolation: The general hostility and prejudice from the white British population in the 1960s.

74720.subject: Literature in English
74720.question_text: Niyi Osundare's "The Leader and the Led" is a fable because of the
74720.explanation:
The poem is classified as a fable because it uses several traditional elements of this literary genre. The poem features a variety of animals, such as the Lion, Hyena, Elephant, Giraffe, Zebra and Warthog, each representing different human leadership traits or personality types. For example:

  • The Lion represents power and strength.

  • The Hyena symbolises greed.

  • The Zebra reflects duplicity or deception.

The "animal kingdom" in the poem serves as an allegory for human society. It specifically critiques the socio-political struggles for leadership in Nigeria and across Africa. The interactions between these animals mirror the power dynamics found in human government and elections.

options.text: use of animals who act as humans

74721.subject: Literature in English
74721.question_text: The persona in Lade Worsonu's "Raider of the Treasure Trove" warns against

74722.subject: Literature in English
74722.question_text:
This question is based on Alex Agyei-Agyiri's Unexpected Joy at Dawn

The temporal setting of the novel is in
74722.explanation:
The novel's temporal setting is defined by two major historical events that reflect the shifting political and economic relationship between the two nations:

The "backstory" and initial separation of the siblings occur during the late 1960s in Ghana. In 1969, the Ghanaian government under Kofi Abrefa Busia enacted the Aliens Compliance Order, which forced non-citizens (including many Nigerians who had lived there for generations) to leave the country. This is when Mama Orojo and her parents were forced back to Nigeria, leaving baby Nii behind in Ghana.

The "present day" events of the novel take place primarily in 1983. During this time, the situation reversed: Nigeria was experiencing economic hardship, and the government of Shehu Shagari ordered the mass deportation of over one million West African migrants, mostly Ghanaians, under the "Ghana Must Go" executive order. Nii Moses Tackie's journey to Nigeria to find his roots occurs against this backdrop.

74723.subject: Literature in English
74723.question_text:
I shall booze and zoom myself home

The diction used in the above excerpt in Onu's "A Government Driver on His Retirement" is
74723.explanation:
Onomatopoeia refers to words that imitate the natural sounds of a thing or suggest their meaning through their sound.

  • "Zoom" imitates the sound of a vehicle moving at high speed. This imitates the persona's haste and excitement as he drives home in his new car.

  • "Booze" (and its variants like "boozy" echoes the sound of drinking or the clinking of glasses during the celebration.

74724.subject: Literature in English
74724.question_text: In Lawrence's "Bat", the poetic persona concludes the poem by stating
74724.explanation: The poem concludes with the persona's clear feeling of disgust and horror toward the creatures. Unlike the swallows he admires earlier in the poem, he describes bats as "pipistrello" and "disgusting," ending with the famous line: "Not for me!"

74725.subject: Literature in English
74725.question_text: Sesay's "The Song of the Women of my Land" is
74725.explanation: Although written in a modern style, the poem functions as a panegyric (a poem of praise). It pays tribute to the resilience, labour and enduring spirit of African women, specifically those who have passed away but whose "song" remains in the soil and culture.

74726.subject: Literature in English
74726.question_text:
This question is based on Buchi Emecheta's Second Class Citizen

It all began like a dream. You know, that sort of dream which seems to have originated from nowhere, yet one was always aware of its existence...

The technique used in the line above is
74726.explanation: The line "It had all begun like a dream..." introduces the backstory of Adah’s childhood. This technique is a flashback (or analepsis), where the author interrupts the chronological flow of the story to show events that happened earlier, providing context for Adah's current situation and her lifelong ambition to move to the United Kingdom.

74727.subject: Literature in English
74727.question_text:
This novel is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger

The bear in the novel symbolically represents
74727.explanation: In the "bears and squirrels" game, Jimmy represents the bear (rugged, aggressive and unpredictable) while Alison represents the squirrel (meek and soft). The game is a psychological retreat from the harshness of their real lives and social class conflicts.

74728.subject: Literature in English
74728.question_text:
This question is based on Wole Soyinka's The Lion and the Jewel.

The division of the play into morning, noon and night signifies unity of

74729.subject: Literature in English
74729.question_text:
Decked with dances by baobabs over balances

The above line in Neto's The Grieved Lands is an example of
74729.explanation:
Alliteration is a literary device where the same consonant sound is repeated at the beginning of several words in close succession. In this specific line:

"Decked with dances by baobabs over balances"

  • The "d" sound repeats in "Decked" and "dances."

  • The "b" sound repeats in "baobabs" and "balances."

74730.subject: Literature in English
74730.question_text:
This question is based on John Osborne's Look Back in Anger

Bullying in the play is revenge tactics on
74730.explanation:
In John Osborne’s play "Look Back in Anger," the protagonist Jimmy Porter’s relentless bullying of his wife, Alison, is a clear example of social class being used as a motivation for revenge tactics.

The play is a cornerstone of "kitchen sink drama" because it focuses on the frustrations of the "Angry Young Man" in post-war Britain. Jimmy’s bullying serves as a weapon in a larger class war:

  • Disparity in Backgrounds: Jimmy comes from a working-class background, while Alison belongs to the upper-middle class. He sees her and her family (especially her father, Colonel Redfern) as symbols of the "complacency" and "insensitive" world that he despises.

  • Targeting the Symbol: Jimmy does not just bully Alison for her personal flaws; he treats her as a representative of her class. By insulting her, he is taking revenge on a social system that he feels has educated him but left him without a meaningful place in society.

  • Provoking a Reaction: He frequently mocks her "pusillanimous" (cowardly) nature and her inability to feel as deeply as he does, which he attributes to her privileged upbringing. His aggression is an attempt to "wake her up" and force her to experience the suffering he associates with the working class.

75031.subject: Literature in English
75031.question_text: The beauty of this poem is built upon its
75031.explanation: In the poem "Akosua Nowa" by Joe de Graft, the extended images of treasure and the gun are central to its meaning and impact. The treasure represents something highly valuable and desirable, while the gun symbolises power, violence and the potential to claim what the speaker desires. The boastfulness of the protagonist, seen in his promise to "shoot my way to it," is intensified by these repeated images, creating a vivid and powerful narrative.

options.text: extended images of treasure and gun

75033.subject: Literature in English
75033.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Fina's character is best described as:
75033.explanation: Fina shows extraordinary strength in overcoming familial, cultural, and global hardships. Her growth reflects resilience and personal evolution.

75035.subject: Literature in English
75035.question_text:
This question is based on HEARTY GARLANDS.

"Flights of vanquished steps" conveys:
75035.explanation: It symbolizes success over struggles, representing the triumph of perseverance, resilience, and determination in the face of hardship.

75038.subject: Literature in English
75038.question_text:
This question is based on NEW TONGUE. What literary device is most prominent in the following lines?

bathing at the back of the house

On a rainy July day
75038.explanation: This line provides a vivid sensory image that invokes feelings of discomfort and exposure. It serves as a symbolic representation of cultural vulnerability.

75042.subject: Literature in English
75042.question_text:
This question is based on THE STONE.

The woman's final sigh symbolises:
75042.explanation: The sigh is a quiet release of grief and a sign that she has fulfilled her final duty to her lover.

options.text: The end of the carving process
The release of her lover's spirit

75044.subject: Literature in English
75044.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

Which character is Ananse's daughter?
75044.explanation: Anansewa is Ananse's only daughter, whom he tries to marry off to the highest bidder among the chiefs.

75046.subject: Literature in English
75046.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Antony: "I will be / A bridegroom in my death, and run into't / As to a lover's bed."

Eros: "Draw that thy honest sword, which thou hast worn / Most useful for thy country."

Antony: "When I did make thee free, sworest thou not then / To do this when I bade thee?" What does this moment between Antony and Eros represent?
75046.explanation: Antony commands Eros to kill him — a test of the servant's loyalty. Eros instead kills himself, prompting Antony to admire him and eventually follow. It's a powerful moment of loyalty and noble self-sacrifice.

options.text: A test of loyalty and self-sacrifice
The dishonour of Eros refusing to fight

75047.subject: Literature in English
75047.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

What is the narrative function of the Kumba Kargbo legend at the beginning of the novel?
75047.explanation: Kumba Kargbo is a forerunner to Fina—she too questions norms, seeks knowledge, and eventually destroys what she wants to save. This mirrors Fina's dilemma of navigating between tradition and modernity.

options.text: To expose the horrors of war.
To symbolise Fina's inner rebellion and uniqueness.

75048.subject: Literature in English
75048.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

In what way does Bendu's relationship with Calvin challenge gender norms?
75048.explanation: Calvin and Bendu relate as equals, without romantic tension or male dominance, emphasizing emotional support and ethical alignment.

options.text: Their partnership is based on mutual respect without traditional gender roles
Calvin is financially dependent on Bendu

75050.subject: Literature in English
75050.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Which element best classifies So the Path Does Not Die as a postcolonial feminist novel?
75050.explanation: The novel confronts both the colonial impact on African societies and the gender-based oppression rooted in tradition—hallmarks of postcolonial feminist discourse.

options.text: Its critique of both colonial legacies and patriarchal customs

75054.subject: Literature in English
75054.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

Which narrative technique best defines the structure of the novel?
75054.explanation: The story unfolds as Lucas narrates his past while sitting by Lucy's hospital bed, using flashbacks.

75055.subject: Literature in English
75055.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

What does the character of Calvin represent in contrast to Terrance Clarke?
75055.explanation: Calvin is a male figure who listens, supports, and acts with integrity—contrasting with Terrance's hypocrisy and self-interest.

75056.subject: Literature in English
75056.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

Who serves as a moral voice and critic of Ananse's schemes?
75056.explanation: Ekuwa frequently challenges Ananse's deceit and selfishness. She acts as a custodian of traditional values and heritage in the society. The plan to deceive the chiefs into thinking Anansewa is dead does not sit well with her, and so Ananse had to send her along with his mother, Aya, off to Nanka so that she does not foil his plan

75058.subject: Literature in English
75058.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

Which of these best describes Ananse?
75058.explanation: Ananse is portrayed as a clever scheer who uses trickery to gain what he wants.

75060.subject: Literature in English
75060.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Caesar: "She shall be buried by her Antony: / No grave upon the earth shall clip in it / A pair so famous."

Dolabella: "Caesar, thy thoughts / Touch their effects in this: thyself art coming / To see perform'd the dreaded act which thou / So sought'st to hinder."

From the excerpt above, Caesar’s statement primarily reveals his
75060.explanation: Caesar acknowledges that Antony and Cleopatra are “a pair so famous,” suggesting that their love and legacy are remarkable and widely recognised. Even in death, he honours their union by allowing them to be buried together. This reflects admiration for their enduring fame and significance.

options.text: regret over his inability to prevent Cleopatra’s death
anger at Dolabella for disobeying his orders
admiration for the enduring fame of Antony and Cleopatra
desire to separate Antony and Cleopatra in death

75061.subject: Literature in English
75061.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

What theme is emphasised when bride prices are accepted from multiple chiefs?
75061.explanation: In the play, Ananse accepts bride prices from multiple chiefs at the same time. He treats his daughter as a means of financial gain. This behaviour reflects greed, as he seeks to maximise profit.

75062.subject: Literature in English
75062.question_text:
This question is based on THE TELEPHONE CALL.

The term "Ultra-Super Global Special" is an example of:
75062.explanation: The exaggerated title parodies how brands or schemes often use grandiose labels to impress.

75063.subject: Literature in English
75063.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

What is the significance of Cobra's polite and religious demeanour after the war?
75063.explanation: Cobra's surface transformation conceals his refusal to take responsibility, complicating ideas of repentance.

options.text: It shows he has been reformed
It disguises unresolved guilt and denial

75065.subject: Literature in English
75065.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Which of the following characters consistently defends African traditions?
75065.explanation: Baramusu is an unyielding traditionalist who insists on the circumcision rite as a marker of true womanhood, even after her granddaughter's death.

75067.subject: Literature in English
75067.question_text:
This question is based on NIGHT.

"Faceless, silent as night thieves" contributes to which theme in the poem?
75067.explanation: This line conveys the silent, creeping threat of Night—like thieves, it brings fear and violation of personal security.

75068.subject: Literature in English
75068.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

What is the deeper symbolic implication of Lucy's coma?
75068.explanation: Lucy's unconscious state mirrors the emotional and generational distance that Lucas seeks to bridge through memory.

options.text: A metaphor for emotional disconnect between generations

75069.subject: Literature in English
75069.question_text: When two statements or comparisons are apparently contradictory, we have an example of:
75069.explanation: A paradox is a figure of speech in which two seemingly contradictory or opposing ideas are combined to reveal a deeper or hidden truth. Although the statements appear illogical at first, they often contain insight or irony that becomes clearer upon reflection.

75073.subject: Literature in English
75073.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

What does Benji's story reveal about the long-term consequences of political silence?
75073.explanation: Benji's unjust execution and forgotten legacy show how silence can erase personal and political history.

options.text: Silence can lead to invisibility and forgotten sacrifices

75075.subject: Literature in English
75075.question_text:
This question is based on SHE WALKS IN BEAUTY.

What does the poet mean by "all that's best of dark and bright"?
75075.explanation: Byron uses light and dark as metaphors to show how her beauty balances grace and mystery, intensity and calmness.

options.text: The woman is both good and evil
She reflects a perfect balance of opposites

75076.subject: Literature in English
75076.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

What does Lucas's refusal to remarry after Isabelle's death reveal about his core values?
75076.explanation: Lucas remains emotionally committed to Isabelle even after her death, showing rare devotion.

options.text: His loyalty and emotional fidelity transcend death
He feels guilty for her illness

75077.subject: Literature in English
75077.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

In Act III, Scene II, Antony blames Cleopatra for:
75077.explanation: After their naval defeat at Actium, Antony accuses Cleopatra of retreating and leading him to follow, effectively blaming her for his disgrace.

options.text: Causing the loss at Actium by fleeing

75078.subject: Literature in English
75078.question_text:
This question is based on ONCE UPON A TIME.

"I have learned to wear many faces / like dresses..." uses which poetic device?
75078.explanation: The comparison between faces and dresses using "like" is a simile, emphasizing how the speaker changes appearances to fit different situations.

75080.subject: Literature in English
75080.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Enobarbus: "Caesar's whole fleet's at sea: / Well spread and almost yare. For he's not dumb, / That tells my departure."

Agrippa: "Let's grant it is not / Amiss to tumble on the bed of Ptolemy; / To give a kingdom for a mirth, to sit / And keep the turn of tippling with a slave..."

What tone is used in the above excerpt and why?
75080.explanation:
The correct answer is D because Agrippa's speech is deeply critical of Antony’s choices.

  • Mockery of Decline: Agrippa mocks Antony's decline by sarcastically referring to his choice to exchange political power and "kingship" for the pleasure found with Cleopatra.

  • Critical Tone: The tone is described as "biting" and critical, highlighting what the Roman characters perceive as Antony's "love-blinded foolishness."

  • Specific Imagery: By mentioning "tippling with a slave" and giving a "kingdom for a mirth," Agrippa emphasizes the contrast between Antony's noble status and his current undignified behavior.

options.text: Dramatic, urging Antony to return to war
Sarcastic, mocking Antony's loss of dignity

75081.subject: Literature in English
75081.question_text:
This question is based on THE BREASTS OF THE SEA.

The image "coelacanth was recaptured" suggests:
75081.explanation: The coelacanth, a fish once thought to be extinct, symbolizes survival and "buried history".

options.text: The rediscovery of something ancient and resilient

75084.subject: Literature in English
75084.question_text:
'Ibadan,

running splash of rust

and gold - flung and scattered

among seven hills like broken

china in the sun.'

J.P. Clark, 'Ibadan'

The poem above is memorable for its:
75084.explanation: The poem is a short, vivid, and emotionally evocative piece that captures the essence of the city. It utilises musical language, imagery, and a compact poetic style, which are hallmarks of lyricism. Rather than narrating a story or praising a hero, the poem expresses the poet's aesthetic feeling and personal impression of the city.

75086.subject: Literature in English
75086.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

What deeper meaning can be attached to Lucas's work on the farm?
75086.explanation: Lucas’s farming serves as a symbol of faithful, repetitive love for his family.

options.text: Work as spiritual discipline and sacrifice

75091.subject: Literature in English
75091.question_text: A central theme in the poem NOT MY BUSINESS is:
75091.explanation: The poem explores the danger of remaining silent in the face of tyranny until it is too late.

75093.subject: Literature in English
75093.question_text:
This question is based on THE NUN'S PRIEST'S TALE.

The final escape of Chanticleer is due to—
75093.explanation: Chanticleer learns from his earlier mistake and uses flattery to trick the fox into speaking, which loosens the fox's grip and allows him to escape.

75227.subject: Literature in English
75227.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

Who is Aya in relation to Ananse?
75227.explanation:
In The Marriage of Anansewa by Efua Sutherland, Aya is Ananse’s mother.

She represents the traditional older generation and reacts with strong emotion, especially when she believes Ananse has died. Her grief scene reflects the cultural expectations of mourning and family honour in the play.

75229.subject: Literature in English
75229.question_text:
This question is based on NIGHT.

The sea in the poem is presented as:
75229.explanation: The sea's fluorescence and movement are quenched by Night's jealous eye, showing Night's dominance over even lively natural forces.

options.text: A symbol of natural vitality subdued by Night
A neutral force in the world

75236.subject: Literature in English
75236.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

'You amble on we can no longer

wait for nature's course

we must deliver

you with force' 

Amelia House, 'Our Sun Rises'

The mood in the lines above is one of
75236.explanation: The poem suggests anger and frustration. Words like "we can no longer wait" and "we must deliver you with force" indicate a sense of urgency and compulsion. This suggests the speaker is no longer willing to tolerate delay—a clear sign of indignation (defined as righteous anger or displeasure).

75239.subject: Literature in English
75239.question_text:
This question is based on NOT MY BUSINESS.

Which literary technique dominates the poem?
75239.explanation: The poem is written in free verse. This means that it has no specific rhythm or rhyme.

75243.subject: Literature in English
75243.question_text:
This question is based on SHE WALKS IN BEAUTY.

The expression "one shade the more, one ray the less" underscores
75243.explanation: Byron emphasises that her beauty is so perfectly balanced that even the slightest alteration (one more shade of darkness or one more ray of light) would diminish its perfection.

options.text: The precision and delicacy of her beauty

75244.subject: Literature in English
75244.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

The temporal setting of the novel is?
75244.explanation: The novel Redemption Road by Elma Shaw is set in post-Civil War Liberia during the era following the end of the Liberian Civil War, which ended in 2003. The story focuses on the aftermath of the war and the struggle for justice and healing in the country, particularly during the administration of Charles Taylor and the period immediately after the conflict. This places the temporal setting around the late 1990s into the 2000s.

75246.subject: Literature in English
75246.question_text:
This question is based on HEARTY GARLANDS.

What is the occasion that inspires the poem?
75246.explanation: The poem serves as a tribute to an elderly man celebrating his 85th birthday.

75260.subject: Literature in English
75260.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Which of the following is NOT a reason why Fina struggles in America?
75260.explanation: Though Fina faces racism, economic pressure, and identity crises, language is not one of her obstacles.

75267.subject: Literature in English
75267.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

What does Lucy's awakening at the novel's end most strongly symbolise?
75267.explanation: Her recovery is a metaphor for healing between generations and the triumph of love over silence.

options.text: Rebirth of hope and emotional reconnection

75274.subject: Literature in English
75274.question_text: In the end, what core message does Redemption Road leave the reader with?
75274.explanation: The novel affirms that redemption, whether personal or national, requires honesty, accountability, and emotional reckoning.

options.text: History should be forgotten to move forward
Healing is possible but depends on courageous confrontation

75278.subject: Literature in English
75278.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

'Beautiful Kareendi, flower of my heart. No one but you can type them. For I want to send them care of the address of your heart, by the post of your heart, to be read by the eye of your heart, thereafter to be kept within your heart, sealed there forever and ever.'

The dominant device in this extract is
75278.explanation:
The extract uses a series of phrases that repeat a structure while slightly varying the words and meaning:

  • “care of the address of your heart”
  • “by the post of your heart”
  • “to be read by the eye of your heart”
  • “thereafter to be kept within your heart, sealed there forever and ever”

Each phrase builds on the previous one to emphasise the intensity of the speaker’s feelings. This technique is called progressive repetition because it repeats the same idea in a slightly varied way to reinforce emotion and create a rhythmic, cumulative effect.

75282.subject: Literature in English
75282.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

How does the novel challenge conventional ideas of masculinity?
75282.explanation: Lucas is a model of tender strength. This counters traditional masculine stoicism.

options.text: By showing Lucas fails as a provider
By showing a man openly supporting a mentally ill spouse

75285.subject: Literature in English
75285.question_text:
Cleopatra (to her attendants):

Give me my robe, put on my crown; I have

Immortal longings in me: now no more

The juice of Egypt's grape shall moist this lip...

Which thematic concern is most evident in this speech?
75285.explanation: Cleopatra speaks with grandeur as she prepares for suicide. "Immortal longings" suggests that death will elevate her beyond human suffering, aligning her with gods. Her dramatic staging of death underlines the theme of death as transcendence and self-assertion.

75292.subject: Literature in English
75292.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

Why is Bendu's abandonment of her child in the Duluma camp significant?
75292.explanation: The act encapsulates her trauma and the psychological fragmentation caused by captivity.

options.text: It highlights her rejection of Cobra's authority
It exposes her lack of maternal instinct
It dramatizes the horrors of war on motherhood and memory

75297.subject: Literature in English
75297.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

'A slight breeze murmured in the air. Grasses swayed as if in resentment. Over in the horizon, just beneath the spectrum of the ascending sun, horizontal brands of red cloud hung menacingly above the tips of the trees and morning air smelled of burnt clay.' 

The Victims by Isidore Okpewho

Effect in the above passage is achieved through the use of
75297.explanation: In the passage from The Victims by Isidore Okpewho, the author creates vivid visual images through descriptive language. Phrases like "grasses swayed as if in resentment," "horizontal brands of red cloud hung menacingly," and "morning air smelled of burnt clay" all evoke strong visual imagery that help the reader imagine the scene in great detail. This makes the use of visual images the most fitting answer.

75300.subject: Literature in English
75300.question_text:
This question is based on THE STONE.

The stone in the poem is primarily a symbol of:
75300.explanation: The headstone represents the desire to preserve the memory of the lost lover, serving as an act of commemoration and emotional finality.

75304.subject: Literature in English
75304.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Fina's insistence on supporting her sister Isa, despite Cammy's protest, stems from:
75304.explanation: Her actions are rooted in the African communal tradition of shared responsibility and kinship loyalty—a theme Cammy, a Westerner, struggles to understand.

75308.subject: Literature in English
75308.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

Where is the play primarily set?
75308.explanation: The action mostly takes place in Ananse's home, where most of the scheming and interactions happen.

75312.subject: Literature in English
75312.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

Ocol rejects the old type.

He is in love with a modern woman

He is in love with a beautiful girl

Who speaks English.'

Okot p'Bitek, 'Song of Lawino'

The writer of the lines above
75312.explanation: In Song of Lawino by Okot p'Bitek, the speaker (Lawino) criticises and mocks Ocol, her husband, for abandoning his traditional roots and his wife (the "old type") in favour of a modern, Westernised woman who speaks English. The tone is satirical and disapproving of Ocol's preference, portraying it as a misguided value judgment.

options.text: shuns the old type of woman
is critical of the modern woman

75314.subject: Literature in English
75314.question_text:
This question is based on PATH OF LUCAS.

Which best reflects Lucas's leadership style within his family?
75314.explanation: Lucas leads by example, choosing sacrifice and empathy over dominance.

75316.subject: Literature in English
75316.question_text:
This question is based on NEW TONGUE.

What does the poem suggest about memory and the past?
75316.explanation: Kamara argues through imagery and tone that rejecting the past equates to erasing one's identity.

options.text: That the past should be rewritten
That the past is a burden
That the past holds identity and should not be erased
That memory is irrelevant to progress

75320.subject: Literature in English
75320.question_text: This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation Comic relief is
75320.explanation:
Comic relief is a literary device used to introduce light-hearted or funny moments into an otherwise serious or tragic story. Its primary functions include:

  • Relieving Tension: It gives the audience a "break" from intense emotional or tragic scenes, making the overall experience more bearable.

  • Contrast: By highlighting a moment of humour, the tragedy that follows or precedes it often feels even more profound and impactful.

  • Humanisation: It can make characters feel more well-rounded and relatable by showing their ability to find humour even in dark circumstances.

options.text: a device used in the theatre where a play ends in marriage
the use of humorous characters speeches or scenes in a tragic work
the use of hearty and wholesome laughter in plays
a figure of speech used in comic theatre

75321.subject: Literature in English
75321.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Enobarbus:

I am alone the villain of the earth, And feel I am so most.

O Antony, Thou mine of bounty, how wouldst thou have paid

My better service, when my turpitude Thou dost so crown with gold!

What emotion primarily drives Enobarbus in this speech?
75321.explanation: In this scene from William Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, Enobarbus is overwhelmed by remorse after deserting Antony to join Caesar. When Antony responds to this betrayal not with anger, but by sending Enobarbus's remaining possessions after him along with extra "bounty" (gifts), Enobarbus is struck by his own "turpitude" (wickedness). He views himself as the "villain of the earth" because he betrayed a leader who remained generous and loyal to him even in defeat.

75322.subject: Literature in English
75322.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

The technique used in bringing the plot of a play to an abrupt end is called:
75322.explanation: Deus ex machina (Latin for "god from the machine") is a dramatic technique in which a seemingly unsolvable problem or complex plot is suddenly and abruptly resolved—often by an unexpected, unlikely intervention (such as a new character, event, or device). This technique can feel artificial or forced, and it usually brings the plot to an abrupt end.

75323.subject: Literature in English
75323.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

When a story is told in a song and passed down by word of mouth, it is called:
75323.explanation: A ballad is a form of narrative verse that is considered a part of oral tradition. Historically, ballads were composed to be sung and were passed from one generation to another by word of mouth. They typically follow a simple rhyme scheme and focus on a single dramatic event or a heroic story.

75325.subject: Literature in English
75325.question_text:
This question is based on THE BREASTS OF THE SEA.

"Fractured chela" refers to:
75325.explanation: A 'chela' is a pincer-like structure; here, it symbolizes fragile remains of the past.

options.text: A delicate remnant of the past

75328.subject: Literature in English
75328.question_text:
This question is based on MARRIAGE OF ANANSEWA.

What style of performance influences the structure of the play?
75328.explanation: The play draws heavily on Anansesem, the traditional Ghanaian storytelling style featuring the trickster spider Ananse.

75332.subject: Literature in English
75332.question_text:
This question is based on THE NUN'S PRIEST'S TALE.

What is the fox's primary strategy in catching Chanticleer?
75332.explanation: The fox uses flattery, appealing to Chanticleer's pride to lure him into singing with his eyes shut.

75334.subject: Literature in English
75334.question_text:
This question is based on THE TELEPHONE CALL.

What does the phrase "We don't deal in money. Experiences are what we deal in" represent?
75334.explanation: The line uses euphemism to hide the truth that there is no actual prize—only a fabricated emotional experience.

75336.subject: Literature in English
75336.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

Which action by Amadu is viewed as a cultural sacrilege?
75336.explanation: Entering the Fafei, a sacred space forbidden to men, is seen as a grave cultural offense by the villagers.

options.text: Allowing his daughter to go to school.
Marrying a woman from another tribe.
Entering the Fafei to stop Fina's circumcision.

75338.subject: Literature in English
75338.question_text:
This question is based on ONCE UPON A TIME.

The line "like a fixed portrait smile" suggests that the speaker's smile is—
75338.explanation: The simile compares the speaker's smile to a static image, emphasizing its lack of authenticity and spontaneity.

75341.subject: Literature in English
75341.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Cleopatra:

O, wither'd is the garland of the war,

The soldier's pole is fall'n: young boys and girls

Are level now with men; the odds is gone,

And there is nothing left remarkable

Beneath the visiting moon.

What is Cleopatra lamenting in this passage?
75341.explanation: Cleopatra mourns Antony's death with poetic metaphors. "Garland of war" and "soldier's pole" symbolise his fallen heroism, showing how with his death, nobility and valour have vanished.

75343.subject: Literature in English
75343.question_text:
This question is based on SO THE PATH DOES NOT DIE.

The abandonment of Musudugu by many women before Kumba Kargbo's birth reflects:
75343.explanation: The rigid rules of Musudugu push many women away; the price of such isolation becomes unbearable, showcasing the mental toll of extreme idealism.

75344.subject: Literature in English
75344.question_text:
This question is based on REDEMPTION ROAD.

How does the novel critique the role of international aid in post-conflict settings?
75344.explanation: While PIP does meaningful work, the novel subtly shows the limits of NGO-led healing in a system lacking deeper structural justice.

options.text: By showing PIP's limitations despite noble intent
By advocating total reliance on foreign assistance
By avoiding mention of external support

75345.subject: Literature in English
75345.question_text:
This question is based on ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA.

Which character says: "The nature of bad news infects the teller."
75345.explanation:
The line “The nature of bad news infects the teller” is spoken by the Messenger in Antony and Cleopatra.

In the scene, the Messenger is reporting troubling updates about political and military developments involving Mark Antony. Before delivering even worse news, he makes this statement to explain a common human reaction: people tend to blame or resent the bearer of bad news, even when the messenger is not responsible for the situation.

This line shows the Messenger’s awareness of the risk he faces in speaking honestly, especially to a powerful and emotionally volatile figure like Antony.

75351.subject: Literature in English
75351.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation

'SINCE I am coming to that Holy roome,

Where, with thy Quire of Saints for evermore

I shall be made thy Musique; As I come

I tune the Instrument here at the dore,

And what I must doe then, thinke here before.'

John Donne, 'Hymn to God my God'

In the stanza above, the poet recognizes that
75351.explanation:
• The "Holy Roome": This represents Heaven or the presence of God.

  • "The Dore": Standing "at the door" is a common literary metaphor for being on the threshold of death.

  • Tuning the Instrument: Donne suggests that his soul (the instrument) must be made ready and "tuned" through prayer and repentance while he is still on Earth, before he joins the "Quire of Saints" (the choir of saints) in eternity.

75353.subject: Literature in English
75353.question_text:
This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation.

A melodramatic play is based on:
75353.explanation:
A melodrama is a dramatic work that exaggerates plot and characters in order to appeal to the emotions. Key features include:

  • Sensationalism: The plot often relies on highly improbable events, suspense, and narrow escapes.

  • Stereotypical Characters: Characters are usually one-dimensional and clearly defined as "good" (heroes/heroines) or "evil" (villains).

  • Emotional Appeal: The primary goal is to evoke strong feelings such as pity, fear, or joy in the audience.
